standard_prerequisites.use: Lifts finiteness of M/fM to finiteness of M using the vanishing of the intersection of the f^nM.

standard_prerequisites.name: The f-divisibility condition on the inverse system
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma lemma-equivalent-f-good (tag 0H39), condition (1)
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the kernel of F_{n+1} -> F_n, which is what makes f a nonzerodivisor on the limit.

core_obligations: Use the cited topology lemma to obtain M/fM contained in H^0(X, F_1), and deduce that M/fM is a finite A-module from the finiteness assumption on Gamma(X, F_1) and Noetherianity of A (proof lines 9316-9318).

Observe that the intersection of the submodules f^nM is zero because f^nM maps to zero in H^0(X, F_n), and apply the cited criterion for finiteness over a complete ring to conclude that M is finite over A (proof lines 9319-9322).

Show f is a nonzerodivisor: if s = (s_n) satisfies fs = 0, then s_{n+1} lies in the kernel of F_{n+1} -> F_n by the f-divisibility condition, so s_n = 0 for every n and hence s = 0 (proof lines 9323-9328).
proof_roadmap: Control M/fM through the first sheaf of the inverse system.
Use vanishing of the intersection of the f^nM and completeness of A to get finiteness of M.
Compute the kernel of multiplication by f from the divisibility condition.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a Noetherian ring A complete with respect to a principal ideal (f), an inverse system of sheaves whose first term has finite global sections and which satisfies the f-divisibility condition has M = lim Gamma(X, F_n) finite over A with f a nonzerodivisor and M/fM the image of M in Gamma(X, F_1). The proof derives the containment M/fM inside H^0(X, F_1) from a cited result, gets finiteness of M/fM from that containment, observes that the intersection of the f^nM is zero by construction, and concludes finiteness of M from the cited complete-ring criterion (proof lines 9316-9322). The final claim is a one-line kernel computation: if fs = 0 then s_{n+1} lies in the kernel of F_{n+1} -> F_n by the divisibility condition (proof lines 9323-9328). H2: combining the two cited finiteness criteria with the explicit description of the kernel is the substance.
